author: sungeunk
title: GPU unit tests fail with a burst of 37 gtest-parallel worker crashes right after fp16_scale_out accuracy mismatch
signature: GPU unit tests accuracy tolerance mismatch in fusion test (val_ref vs val_opt difference exceeds tolerance in fusion_test_common.hpp) followed by burst of concurrent gtest-parallel worker processes exiting with code 3|Flaky Test

failed_jobs.name: GPU unit tests
failed_jobs.symptom: fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 fails accuracy check by 3.05e-05 past tolerance, then 37 later tests crash with exit code 3

key_errors: C:\actions-runner\_work\openvino\openvino\openvino\src\plugins\intel_gpu\tests\unit\fusions\fusion_test_common.hpp(90): error: The difference between val_ref[i] and val_opt[i] is 3.0517578125e-05, which exceeds tolerance

FAILED TESTS (37/29306): ... convolution_grouped_gpu.base/... returned with exit code 3, basic/convolution_random_smoke_test.* returned with exit code 3 (x36), fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 returned with exit code 1
root_cause: This is the same recurring GPU unit test flake tracked under pattern 502c01bffd8f35db (7 prior occurrences between 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14, now recurring again). fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 fails an fp16 accuracy comparison in fusion_test_common.hpp by a tiny margin (3.05e-05), consistent with borderline floating-point tolerance sensitivity in fp16 pooling+scale fusion rather than a correctness regression. A burst of 36 additional tests (mostly basic/convolution_random_smoke_test.* and a grouped convolution case) then exit with code 3 instead of completing normally, which is the gtest-parallel worker-crash signature seen in prior occurrences of this same pattern - these are concurrent worker processes that die early in the run (around test indices 1-36) rather than genuine per-test assertion failures. The merge in this run integrates an oneDNN submodule bump (PR #39899, 'onednn rls-v3.15-pc integration'), a 1-line submodule pointer change with no GPU-plugin source changes, so it is very unlikely to be the root cause of this specific flake; it most likely bisects a lucky/unlucky scheduling window on the Windows GPU runner.
reproduction_steps: On a Windows GPU runner: build ov_gpu_unit_tests, then run via gtest-parallel: python gtest_parallel.py --gtest_filter=fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 ov_gpu_unit_tests.exe. The failure is intermittent (accuracy margin is borderline), so multiple repeated runs may be needed to reproduce; the worker crashes among the first ~36 scheduled tests are similarly non-deterministic and tied to parallel worker startup/resource contention rather than a specific input.
recommended_actions: Review the pass/fail tolerance used in fusion_test_common.hpp for fp16 pooling+scale fusion tests (currently failing by 3.05e-05); consider loosening fp16 comparison tolerance slightly if this is a known borderline case.

Investigate why exactly the first ~36 scheduled gtest-parallel worker tests (convolution_grouped_gpu, convolution_random_smoke_test variants) intermittently exit with code 3 early in the run on Windows GPU runners - check for GPU driver/resource contention during gtest-parallel worker startup.

If this pattern keeps recurring (now 8 total observations), consider marking fusings_gpu/pooling_f32_scale.fp16_scale_out/1 as a known-flaky test or quarantining it pending a tolerance fix, to stop blocking merge-queue/post-commit CI.
prevention_strategies: Add tolerance-margin logging/telemetry to fusion_test_common.hpp so near-miss accuracy failures (within 2x tolerance) are flagged distinctly from genuine regressions. Track gtest-parallel worker exit code 3 occurrences separately from assertion failures in CI reporting so bursts like this are auto-classified as infra flakiness rather than requiring manual investigation each time.
historical_context: Identical signature (502c01bffd8f35db) recorded 7 times between 2026-11-13T17:54:36Z and 2026-11-14T07:30:39Z across unrelated commits, confirming this is a long-standing intermittent GPU unit test issue on Windows runners, not something introduced by the current commit.
